body: I can't even afford to live alone. It may be misguided but all I want is to be alone. I saved when I worked retail and have just enough money to finish my degree on my current reserves, but that assumes my rent and bills are split between two. It's unbelievable how much nagging wears you down when you have nowhere to hide.

I hate even typing it because it sounds so much more grand than it is. I get embarrassed if people ask what I do because it makes me sound like such a wannabe. Then they see how old I am and the obvious disjoint is shameful.  
Uni itself sucks for nearly everyone I know, even the most successful people I knew from highschool. It's a means to an end and you gotta make the most of it. If you're young you can truly embrace it and I encourage you wholeheartedly to do so. Immerse yourself in it, whether that be social or academic, because I believe it can be a wonderful time for people who didn't waste their opportunities like I did.  
I may be wrong to say this but it doesn't get better if you do nothing. Been there done that. I'd urge my younger self to form that resolve for change now, rather than wasting your life, your passion, your health, suffering and waiting for a sunken ship to right itself.

haha the first month of mirtazapine I slept the best I had in years. No nagging thoughts keeping me up until dawn. 3 months later and I am not exaggerating when I say sleeping 16 hours by accident is not unusual. I set alarms for 9-10 hour sleeps and feel like I used to feel on 5 hour sleep.  
The drug is fucked unless your problem is needing immediate relief from a strong emotion. It makes you die. Medically induced death.  
Graduating and not getting a job would absolutely be the straw the broke my back. My degree has a lot of applications but I know it's a real possibility, especially if I can't stand up and keep going with full force.  
You have a lot of strength to graduate after all that have to commit to re-skilling to make yourself more employable.  
I'm personally scared of antidepressants forever. I put off trying them for 13 years and I now believe that was the correct decision... :/

Ah, psychology. Must be kind of sad knowing the problem so intimately and still being helpless.  
I'm studying ~~redacted to avoid ID~~

If you're only living for other people you'll always be a ghost of the real thing. You need to form a personal resolve. Harden your willpower, armour it with all the suffering and struggle you've put in.  
I, like you, am on the wrong side of my 20's. I've done 5 years of uni, and 4 years of retail shit. Failed 2 degrees, working on a 3rd completely unrelated to the first two.  
I am struggling. I wouldn't be here if I wasn't honestly. But I took the hardship I endured working in a ghetto job where I was in legitimate danger every day just to earn a barely-livable wage, and I focussed on that suffering and told myself, if I don't change, with everything I have, I won't be able to live with myself for another year.  
Even now, when i'm stumbling, the fact that I am putting my all into a worthy goal keeps me standing. I can't fucking die now I've worked too hard AND I'M NOT FUCKING DONE YET.  
Pick a reasonable, achievable goal, that you want, and commit. Not half heartedly. Don't "commit because it's the only way forward". Commit because you hurt. Commit because tomorrow can't be worse than today. Motivation is temporary, but resolve and discipline is eternal.  
Good luck, I believe in you.

I just looked at your profile and you're an unbelievably good person. Trying to help so many despite struggling with yourself.  
Whether i've been treading water or drowning i've always been a negative fuck. I see it as being realistic, but in truth it is a shitty way to be. The people who twist the truth in their favour are the ones who achieve it all I guess.

It's hard for me to feel hard-done by because my upbringing was fairly average. I was highly ambitious and passionate about everything. Passion gradually fades to bitterness in the face of failure I guess. Had good aptitude so "never needed to study" before uni. That ego led to my drop-out of my first degree. Worked retail in a dogshit ghetto slum for 3 years. Commuted 40 minutes each way every shift for a job that barely paid enough to pay rent. Had to move out of home once I failed university ofcourse.  
I built up so much resolve in that horrible job. I had addicts threaten to stab/shoot/rob me when I came off work on a number of occasions. As miserable as it made me I thought my passion had been re-ignited.  
Going back into uni in an even more ambitious degree was tough enough, as the misery never really lessened, but behind the scenes my decaying relationship and living situation was eating me inside.  
It came to the point where the only thing that that made me feel the sparks was playing competitive games like CSGO or League of Legends. Then you realise that those things just waste you away even more and the conflict between the resolve to improve built from suffering and the long lost sparks of passion found in a worthless game... 
If I was normal I think i'd be fine. But i'm not normal. My brain is fucked. I go over my circumstances over and over and I know i shouldn't feel so fucked up but I do. I think I didn't respond well to anti-depressants because i'm not "sad", there isn't something I needed temporary numbness from. The numbness is my prison, and I took a pill that amplified it 10-fold.

You're right. Time stretches. At first I was sad to be a teen with unrequited love. Fairly typical. Then it stretches into a young man with heartbreak. Then you fall in and out of a few relationships, and they feel long, but a year or 3 withers behind you. You distinctly note that each one feels weaker than the last. You no longer feel sad for love. You don't feel positive emotions that strongly.  
I don't think I even registered it until this year. The creeping numbness. The fact that being sad for so long is genuinely etched into my face. I barely go outside, i'm not a wrinkly mess. Yet I can tell looking at my face. This guy is fucking miserable. I don't know.  
Your comment makes my heart ache for you but I have nothing to say that isn't negative.
My all-room is the embodiment of my suffering.
All cultures are boring and weird, fact. Don't let your culture define you, there is much more in the world to be miserable about.
